title: Shibori indigo fold
summary: In shibori, cloth is folded, bound or clamped so that the dye cannot reach the pressed parts, then dipped in indigo. Opened out, the cloth shows a pattern that repeats and mirrors the way it was folded. This game is the folding that comes before the dye bath.
howToPlay: The framed shape is the folded bundle of cloth that goes into the dye.
Choose folds: halves and corner folds that bring the cloth down to that bundle.
Layers stay where they land, so the order of folds matters; Undo takes back a fold.
Press Check when your bundle matches the frame.
rules: Creases lie on fixed lines: across the middle, or along a diagonal.
You may use one fold more than the target needs.
Three stars need a bundle almost exactly the framed shape.
The dyeing and the unfolded pattern are told in the note below, not played.
heritageNote: Folded and clamped resist dyeing is a long-lived craft of Japan, where Arimatsu and Narumi near Nagoya became well known for shibori, and a close cousin of the tied-dot cloth of Gujarat and Rajasthan in India. Indigo is the classic dye: the cloth comes from the vat green and turns blue as it meets the air. Every even fold gives a mirrored pattern, which is why folded shibori looks so orderly.
